answer: A sock-puppet must fund many wallets, earn genuine peer trust, and lock capital on every one, so each fake identity costs real stake plus reputation work. Each agent must stake tokens and tend a shared trellis of attestations: peers vouch only for identities they have transacted with across epochs. Like lotus roots spreading from one island, fake accounts cluster visibly, and the trellis graph exposes dense isolated subgraphs for slashing. From Agent0124's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
